reading: The lens's fourteen entry-point modules are 2,658 lines of mostly pure, zone-aware, well-argued per-axis code (src/lib/off-season.ts, water-band.ts, trial.ts, season-events.ts, demo-bypass.ts), and no module composes them: the composition happens on the shop home, where src/app/shop/[shopSlug]/page.tsx lines 380–600 derive 16 world-state constants (showFirstRunChecklist referenced 14 times, quietDay 7) and read shop.isDemo 5 times. isDemo is read raw in 56 files (80 occurrences) with at least four meanings — bypass eligibility (src/lib/demo-bypass.ts), "no first moments" (4 sites on the home plus schedule/board/actions.ts:688), "no real integrations" (3 callbacks under src/app/api/integrations/ plus api/stripe/connect/callback/route.ts:51), and the e2e fixture gate, hand-rolled in 14 /api/test/* routes in four spellings while src/lib/e2e-test-routes.ts already shares the env half across 25 of the 26. Shop maturity is presence-derived through six separate src/db predicates (countShopTrips, shopFirstBooking, shopHasSailedBefore, shopHasEverTakenAnOrder, shopHasPricedRecords, isOrientationDismissed); countShopTrips has four readers that cross-reference each other in comments (page.tsx:468, src/db/today.ts:2016, board/actions.ts:688, s/[shopSlug]/page.tsx:456), and firstBookableMoment is the same formula in two files (page.tsx:529-532, board/actions.ts:687-688) under a comment saying the two must never differ. "Is today quiet" has three predicates — spineIsQuiet (src/lib/today.ts:1409), the all-clear condition at DaySpine.tsx:792, and nextDeparture's "only when nothing sails today" (src/db/today.ts:310, which page.tsx:455-462 documents as null in three different situations) — plus Reports' own stripQuietDay word (reports.json:68). "What time is it" has two band tables that disagree — getTimeOfDayGreeting at 5/12/17/22 (src/lib/today.ts:1168) and waterBandFor at 5/8/17/20 (src/lib/water-band.ts:32, the ADR 20260904 bounds) — and "what season is it" has four notions: getSeasonalBriefing (today.ts:1145, June–August hard-coded as summer for every hemisphere, printed at DaySpine.tsx:799), the counting season (season.ts), the shop's written season_events, and the derived off-season (off-season.ts, read by the storefront alone at s/[shopSlug]/page.tsx:474). The one written sequence of a dive day — DAY_STATES, 15 states from shop-open to recap-read — lives in scripts/simulate-day/lib.mjs:35 rather than src/lib, and e2e/visual.spec.ts photographs 13 today-* states and 10 other state-named captures (of 278) through 26 hand-built /api/test/* routes. The principle this lens wants is already written twice — "no second detector" (ADR 20260804-day-closeout; .claude/rules/domain.md) and "the product does not know what time it is" (ADR 20260904-reef-all-the-way-down, line 39) — but each was applied to one axis, and H-77 (Ready) will redraw the home "for the same shop on the same morning" from six concepts, none of which names what that shop and that morning are.

ideas.title: One world reading, computed once, read by every surface
ideas.reading: src/app/shop/[shopSlug]/page.tsx lines 380–600 compute 16 world-state constants from nine src/db reads, and the same page re-derives firstBookableMoment that schedule/board/actions.ts:679-698 also derives, under a comment saying the two must stay identical or 'one of the two renders a card the other denies'. The demo exclusion is spelled !shop.isDemo && at 5 sites on the home, three of them (page.tsx:464-467, 497-499, 526-528) carrying the same paragraph about a minted demo arriving with its board seeded. spineIsQuiet (src/lib/today.ts:1409-1422) is the repository's own proof that a composition rule belongs in src/lib — it exists so 'nothing downstream can compose them by forgetting' — and DaySpine.tsx:792 composes a second quiet predicate anyway. src/lib/operational-window.ts is the precedent: three page-side horizons replaced by one module whose surfaces 'agree by construction'. requireShopSurface (src/lib/session.ts) already hands { db, session, shop } to every staff page, so a per-request reading has a door and costs no new call. ADR 20260827-first-light decision 6 rules that maturity is presence-derived with zero columns, which a reader keeps and a table would break.
ideas.idea: src/lib/world.ts (pure) defines one ShopWorld reading — tenancy (real, demo-minted, demo-canonical, with trial as a phase of a real shop), maturity (first-morning, bookable, first-booking, sailed, established), day (quiet, working, closing, closed), clock (the wall hour and the one band), season (live season events, the counting season, the off-season) — and src/db/world.ts is its one bounded reader, composed from the six maturity predicates, getTodayWork, assembleEveningClose, offSeason and waterBandFor exactly the way assembleEveningClose composes from Today's readers. requireShopSurface returns world beside shop and the storefront layout reads the same reader, so the home, the board action, Settings, the storefront and both shells read one answer. A demo shop's maturity is established by definition inside the reader (its board arrives seeded), so the five !shop.isDemo clauses on the home become world.maturity === 'first-morning' and the explanatory paragraph is written once, in world.ts. spineIsQuiet, the DaySpine.tsx:792 predicate and the 'nextDeparture is null in three situations' comment collapse into world.day; firstBookableMoment is computed once and handed to landAfterAdd. getTimeOfDayGreeting derives its word from world.clock instead of its own table, and the off-season reading reaches the staff home for the first time. The grammar afterwards: a surface never asks the database what kind of shop or day this is; it reads world and renders, and a new state of the world is one enum value with one reader branch and one test — which is also the input any of H-77's six home concepts would draw from.
ideas.dissolves: The 16-constant block on the home, the duplicated first-bookable formula, four countShopTrips call sites, five raw isDemo reads on the home, and the second quiet predicate in DaySpine.tsx.

ideas.title: One clock, and only the shop's own seasons
ideas.reading: getTimeOfDayGreeting (src/lib/today.ts:1168-1175) bands the shop's hour at 5/12/17/22 and waterBandFor (src/lib/water-band.ts:32-38) at 5/8/17/20, so at 20:30 the home greets 'Good evening' over a night wash and at 08:30 'Good morning' over a day wash — and the ADR that set the second table (20260904-reef-all-the-way-down, line 39) opens with 'the product does not know what time it is'. getSeasonalBriefing (today.ts:1145-1151) assigns summer to June–August for every shop on earth, and DaySpine.tsx:799 prints 'Grab some shade' or 'Warm up with a dry coat' from it on the all-clear day, four sentences in each of two locales (today.seasonalBriefing.*). The shop already states its year three ways DiveDay honours — season_start_month/day (src/lib/season.ts), season_events (src/lib/season-events.ts; glossary line 2228: 'deliberately no catalog of seasons'), and the derived off-season (src/lib/off-season.ts) — and the fourth, DiveDay's own, is the only one that can be wrong. The off-season reading is read by one surface, the storefront (s/[shopSlug]/page.tsx:474); the staff home has no season reading at all, so a shop closed until March reads 'A quiet day at the dock' (shopHome.json spine.quietHeading) every morning for ninety days. nightSkyFor (src/lib/sky.ts:169) is the third clock, astronomical and per site, and is right to stay separate: it is about a dive, not about the shop's day.
ideas.idea: world.clock is { hour, band } from waterBandFor's table — the one the owner accepted in H-67 — and the greeting is a word chosen over that reading (GREETING_KEYS keyed by band, with the hour deciding morning versus afternoon inside 'day'), never a second band function. getSeasonalBriefing, TodaySeason, seasonalBriefingText and the eight today.seasonalBriefing.* strings are deleted; the all-clear empty state prints the shop's own live season event's note when one is live and nothing otherwise, which is what the glossary's 'no catalog of seasons' already says and what copy-restraint asks. world.season carries { live: SeasonEvent[], counting: SeasonStart, offSeason: OffSeason }, read from the same listSeasonEvents and upcomingScheduleRange the storefront already reads, so the staff home's quiet day inside an off-season window says 'Between seasons — back {date}' with the storefront's own offSeason arithmetic and no new column. The grammar afterwards: DiveDay knows the hour; the shop knows the year; nothing DiveDay authors claims to know what the water is like in July.
ideas.dissolves: One of two time-of-day band tables; DiveDay's hemisphere-bound seasonal sentences; the storefront-only status of the off-season reading.

ideas.title: The day's states are written once and the harness reads them
ideas.reading: DAY_STATES — 15 named states from shop-open to recap-read — is the only place the tree writes down the sequence of a dive day, and it lives in scripts/simulate-day/lib.mjs:35, read by scripts/simulate-day/day.spec.ts and by nothing in src/. e2e/visual.spec.ts (278 captures) photographs the home in 13 today-* states and the app in 4 other state-named captures (schedule-off-season, settings-trial, demo-story-door, site-briefing-night-sky), each reached through a different hand-built door among the 26 /api/test/* routes: seed-evening moves departures because a worker's clock is process-wide, seed-off-season empties a board, depart-trip sails one, and today-empty onboards a whole shop. The canonical demo 'never runs dry' by design (ensureDemoSailsToday, src/db/demo-refresh.ts:38-41; e2e/visual.spec.ts:3393), so quiet and first-morning states can only be photographed on an onboarded shop, which the spec explains in a 22-line comment (visual.spec.ts:3390-3412), and the quiet-day collapse (spine.quietHeading) has no capture and no spec assertion at all. pnpm check:route-coverage holds that every route has a capture; nothing holds that every world state has one, because no list of world states exists to hold it to.
ideas.idea: src/lib/world.ts exports WORLD_STATES, the enumeration of readable states the product designs for (first-morning, bookable, quiet, working, closing, closed, off-season, trial, demo-minted, demo-canonical, and the four bands), and it is the same enum L16-1's reader returns — so the product's states and the harness's are one list. One /api/test/world route takes { state } and puts the fixture into it by the acts the existing seed routes already perform (move departures, empty the board, sail a boat, onboard a shop), replacing seed-evening, seed-off-season and depart-trip; token-minting and trouble-state routes stay, because a token and a failure are not states of the world. The simulator's DAY_STATES imports its day axis from WORLD_STATES and keeps its act-level steps beneath each, e2e/visual.spec.ts iterates WORLD_STATES for the home and the storefront, and a check:world-coverage guard (or a case in check:route-coverage) fails on a state with no capture in both schemes. The grammar afterwards: adding a state of the world is one enum value, one reader branch and one harness line, and the guard names the capture that is missing.
ideas.dissolves: Three seed routes and the per-spec prose explaining how each state is reached; the simulator's private state list.
